entries.title: Clock Tower
entries.definitive_edition: Clock Tower: Rewind Steam PC release for the main run; The First Fear for variant-content sampling

emulation.emulator: Native Rewind PC release; DuckStation for The First Fear; bsnes/Mesen-S for Super Famicom comparison
emulation.notes: Use Rewind on PC for the primary route. Use PlayStation emulation only to inspect The First Fear variant content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC/console Rewind presentation, with historical versions available for comparison.

primary.version: Clock Tower: Rewind Steam PC release
primary.why: Clock Tower: Rewind is the best primary route because it is the official modern international release of the original game, available on PC and consoles with localization and modern release support.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Clock Tower: Rewind on Steam for the cleanest capture route, or use the Switch/PlayStation/Xbox versions if preferred. Sample the Japan-only PlayStation version The First Fear separately if you want its older variant additions.

secondary.exclusive_content: Clock Tower: The First Fear is an updated Japan-only version with a new dagger weapon, new room, minor scenario additions, FMV scenes, and minor graphical improvements.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample Clock Tower: The First Fear on PlayStation if you specifically want that Japan-only variant content.
secondary.why: Rewind is the modern official primary, but The First Fear has variant content worth preserving as secondary.

all_releases.reason: skip: historically important original, but superseded for access by Rewind and for variant content by The First Fear.

all_releases.fidelity: Clock Tower: The First Fear, an updated Japan-only PlayStation version with added weapon/room/scenario/FMV material.
all_releases.reason: secondary: variant content exists, but Rewind is the best modern official primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only Windows 95 port of The First Fear era release.
all_releases.reason: skip: historical PC port with no sourced advantage over the current Rewind PC release.

all_releases.fidelity: Monochrome handheld port with HUD changes and no pause option.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable historical version, but lower fidelity and no primary-run advantage.

all_releases.platform: Wii Virtual Console / Wii U Virtual Console / PlayStation Network
all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only digital rerelease routes for earlier versions.
all_releases.reason: skip: official historical digital access, but region-constrained and superseded by Rewind.

all_releases.platform: Windows PC / PlayStation 5 / PlayStation 4 / Xbox Series X|S / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
all_releases.fidelity: Clock Tower: Rewind modern official release, translated outside Japan for the first time and available on PC plus modern consoles.
all_releases.reason: primary: best official modern route and broadest access, while the PS1 variant is preserved as secondary.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Rewind is the best modern official route and localization, but the Japan-only PlayStation The First Fear version has documented variant additions.

entries.remaster_caveats: Rewind is an enhanced/emulated modern release of the original game, not a full remake; The First Fear remains a distinct older updated variant.

entries.title: Clock Tower (1996)

emulation.notes: Use DuckStation with an owned PlayStation disc image for the primary capture route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS1 presentation with emulator-side resolution, PGXP, and filtering options.

primary.why: The 1996 Clock Tower sequel is a PlayStation-only release with no sourced official remaster, PC port, or modern rerelease, so the original PlayStation version through DuckStation is the complete and highest-practical-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play an owned PlayStation copy on original hardware or use DuckStation with an owned disc image for cleaner capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PlayStation release; DuckStation can improve capture quality from an owned copy.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced commercial platform, preserving the complete original release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No alternate release with higher official fidelity or exclusive content was identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced official remaster, remake, PC port, or modern rerelease was identified.
